title: Hide the "Favourites" section when it is empty.
line: Kickoff no longer opens on an empty Favorites page: the category is hidden until you add a favorite, and All Applications is shown instead.
explanation: Kickoff's sidebar always has Favorites as its first category and every reset (opening, closing, Home key) goes back to row 0, so with no favorites it opened on a blank page. The sidebar list now takes a first selectable row: when there are no favorites the Favorites row is collapsed and All Applications becomes the default, Up/Home/PageUp stop there, and removing the last favorite switches to All Applications. The row shows again while an app is being dragged so it stays a drop target for adding the first favorite.

commits.message:
applets/kickoff: hide the Favorites category when it is empty

Kickoff always opened on the Favorites category, even when there were no
favorites and the page was blank. Now the category is hidden while empty
and All Applications is shown instead; it reappears while dragging an app.

BUG: 474390

media.caption: No favorites: Kickoff opens on an empty Favorites page
No favorites: Favorites is hidden and Kickoff opens on All Applications
Removing the last favorite leaves Kickoff on a blank Favorites page
Removing the last favorite switches to All Applications and hides Favorites
Dragging an app shows Favorites again so the first favorite can be dropped there

reviews.text: Collapsing the empty Favorites row in QML while keeping it as a drop target during drag-and-drop, paired with a firstIndex property on KickoffListView, is a clean approach that avoids rebuilding RootModel or shifting category indices. However, ApplicationsPage still hardcodes stackView's initialItem to preferredFavoritesViewComponent and appsModelRow to 0, which can leave the content area blank on initial load when Kickoff starts with zero favorites and rootModel is already populated. In addition, KickoffListView's header MouseArea still accepts targetIndex >= 0 instead of respecting root.firstIndex.
changes: In ApplicationsPage.qml, initialize stackView's appsModelRow and initialItem based on whether favoritesModel.count > 0 (or explicitly sync stackView when sideBarItem loads) instead of hardcoding preferredFavoritesViewComponent and appsModelRow: 0, and verify on a fresh plasmashell start with 0 favorites.

In KickoffListView.qml, update the header MouseArea onEntered check to respect root.firstIndex (e.g. targetIndex >= root.firstIndex) so hovering the top margin with switchCategoryOnHover enabled cannot select the hidden Favorites row at index 0.

reviews.text: Does what the reporter and Nate asked: with no favorites the Favorites row is hidden and Kickoff opens on All Applications, removing the last favorite switches away, and the row comes back as a drop target while dragging an app (all shown in the media). Keeping RootModel untouched and hiding the row in QML via a firstIndex is the least invasive approach, and every place that reset to row 0 (open/close, count change, Home/PageUp/Up) is covered. Minor nits: the collapsed row still takes the list spacing so All Applications sits ~4 px lower than Favorites did, and the whole category list shifts down by one row when a drag starts.
